reference: benchmarks/machine_count: the same model and search; Erlang C for the M/M/c queue, lambda = 1/120 per s, E(S) = 90 s (Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), equations 5.1 and 5.3): 1 till waits 270 s at utilization 0.75, 2 tills 162/11 s at 0.375, and 3 to 5 tills fall below the limit 0.35 (0.25, 0.1875, 0.15), so the best is 2

benchmarks/machine_count: the same model and search; Erlang C for the M/M/c queue, lambda = 1/120 per s, E(S) = 90 s (Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), equations 5.1 and 5.3): the best, 2 tills, confirmed with 30 replications: Pi_W = 9/44, E(W) = Pi_W/(c mu - lambda) = 162/11 s

benchmarks/machine_count: the same model and search; Erlang C for the M/M/c queue, lambda = 1/120 per s, E(S) = 90 s (Adan and Resing, Queueing Systems (2015), equations 5.1 and 5.3): the best, 2 tills: utilization lambda E(S)/c = 0.75/2 = 0.375
